review.verdict: Reads clearly as "human says no, money flows to AI anyway," but a clipped/out-of-safe-area funnel, an illegible overlapping money label, and an invisible ticket prop drag the average to roughly 3.4 — just below the publish bar.
revisionNotes: Funnel/vent is clipped by the top edge and the lint flags it outside the safe area (y 4…258) — scale the funnel to ~0.85 and nudge it down so the vent clears the canvas top with margin.
"MORE MONEY" label overlaps the pink funnel spout and loses legibility where the colors match — recolor the label to r-ink/navy or raise its offset fully above the triangle.
The ticket prop (attached to bot, offset 10,-140) isn't visibly rendered — bring it forward in z-order and reposition into the robot's outstretched hand so 'holding out a ticket' actually reads.

Robot's arms stretch to touch both the agent and the server rack at once, reading as gripping neighbors rather than offering a ticket — set one arm toward the agent holding the ticket, tuck or lower the other.
Add a simple raw counter/desk shape between agent and bot so the scene reads as an airline check-in instead of a generic street encounter.

This human+robot+server-building triptych is close in composition to several recent pieces (Business As Usual, REJECTED, New Name) — vary the framing, e.g. angle the building or break the strict left-right triad, for more novelty.

review.verdict: Marginal pass: the robot-rejected-at-a-counter-while-money-pours-into-a-datacenter joke reads clearly and the cast and kindness are solid, but a large empty bottom third, an ambiguous arm gesture, a half-hidden ticket, and the missing 'NO AI' gate/stamp keep it from feeling fully resolved.
revisionNotes: Fill the empty bottom third of the frame (roughly y=850–1080 is bare paper texture); ground the scene with a shadow line or small prop so the composition uses the full square.

The agent's arm reads as a diagonal rest/point rather than the brief's 'stop-sign hand'; raise the hand prop to scale ~1.1 and angle it vertically above the counter so the rejection gesture is unmistakable without relying on the NO bubble.

The ticket prop is tucked behind the counter edge and reads as a badge on the robot's torso, not something being held out; move it left/forward (offset further from 'bot', scale 1.2) so it's clearly visible.

The brief's 'gate stamped NO AI' with a bouncing rejected request and single pink highlight never made it into the scene; add that gate near the counter to anchor the rejection to the airline/gate metaphor instead of a generic speech bubble.

Pink accent is scattered across the robot's joints, the funnel triangle, and the steam puffs, diluting the single fluorescent-pink highlight the style brief calls for; reserve it for one focal element (e.g. the NO AI stamp).

The human + robot + server-rack-building layout is close to several recent sloppers (person/robot pair beside a datacenter with a stat or label); vary the framing or add an airport-specific prop (turnstile, luggage) to stand out.
